entries.title: Band 6 of the official training_features.tif is a radiometric band mis-tagged as magnetic
entries.what_it_is: Band 6 carries data_category='magnetic_data' and description='Tilt angle or total curvature - magnetic field derivative for edge detection' in the organiser's own file. It is the GeoDAWN aeroradiometric total-count (TC) grid. src/gems52/features.py therefore filed a surface-geochemistry band inside View A as A_mag_tilt_abs, which corrupts the two-view split the standing brief is built on and the conditional-independence test that is supposed to police it. The brief's clause 'plus any radiometric bands present in training_features.tif' resolves to one band, not to none.
entries.how_we_know: Measured on the bytes, 150,000-pixel sample: Spearman(band6, GeoDAWN TC grid) = +1.0000; Spearman(band6, K+Th+U) = +0.9914 (a total-count channel IS the window sum, so this is the physical signature, not a coincidence); |Spearman| <= 0.149 against all five magnetic bands in the same file (TMI -0.0250, TMI up-continued 150 m +0.0079, TMI horizontal gradient -0.1489, TMI vertical gradient +0.0214, RTP -0.0914). A magnetic-field derivative cannot be uncorrelated with the magnetic field. Band 6 is also strictly positive (min 2.953, max 88.573) while a tilt angle is bounded by +/- pi/2. Official source for the TC grid: Glen & Earney 2024, USGS data release, https://doi.org/10.5066/P93LGLVQ.
entries.disposition: corrected - src/gems55/radlayers.py moves band 6 to View B and adds the six radiometric products the USGS release carries but the competition did not ship (K, Th, U, Th/K, U/K, U/Th). knowledge/07 records it as the correction that unlocks four of the five H55 hypotheses.

entries.title: The README states the grid as '3730 x 3292', which is height x width
entries.what_it_is: rasterio reports width=3292, height=3730 for every official raster; grid.SHAPE = (3730, 3292) is (rows, cols). Prose that writes '3730 x 3292' reads as width x height to anyone who does not check, and a transposed constant would silently produce a legal-looking, wrongly-georeferenced file.

entries.title: |G| is not published, but it is recoverable from the metric and our own scored history
entries.what_it_is: The number of hidden public-test truth pixels drives the credit bar and therefore the file size, and the organiser does not publish it. knowledge/05 fixed the budget at K=37654 'to match the 0.2778 file's footprint mass', i.e. inherited it from an unrelated submission rather than deriving it.
entries.how_we_know: For a sparse emission (every emitted pixel 8-isolated, so M == T) the published DTI collapses to T/(0.2*S + 0.8*|G|) with one unknown; T <= |G| then gives |G| >= 0.2*DTI*S/(1 - 0.8*DTI) per submission. Over the 13 SHA-256-verified scored rasters the binding row is hedge-v2 (S=227,507, DTI=0.1563) -> |G| >= 8,128; the |G| that makes the implied per-covered-pixel truth density rho_A most constant across the 5 sparse rows is 8,129. knowledge/01's independent loss decomposition of the 0.2778 file gave 8,000 (tax 6,757 / credit 3,870 / miss 3,304), i.e. two different derivations agree to 1.6 %.
entries.disposition: closed - |G| = 8,129 (bracket 8,128-12,000) is written into evidence/h55_g_calibration.json and is the number the H55 credit bar uses. Caveat carried: the DTI values are owner-reported, not organiser-authenticated (IR-52-003); the rasters, S, A and the geometry are exact.

entries.title: The family's best submission spends only 86% of the kernel's placement efficiency
entries.what_it_is: One isolated emitted pixel can contribute at most 9.380298 of kernel-weighted coverage A (the disc weight sum, enumerated exactly). A/S = 8.044 for the 0.2778 file (86% of the ceiling), 7.956 for d2-8, 6.564 for d1-5, 3.813-3.937 for the contiguous h19/h16 files (41%), 1.664 for the placeholder (18%). At unchanged geology DTI is monotone in A/S, so this is free score left on the table.
entries.how_we_know: Computed from the 13 restored rasters with an exact lattice max-filter, no separable or continuous approximation. Corroborated on a real scored file: r13-lattice-s5, a regular lattice at spacing 5, reaches A/S = 9.361 = 99.8% of the ceiling. Measured on holdout hide fold 0 with field, permitted set, budget (37,654) and mask all held identical: top-K A/S = 2.233 -> DTI 0.03196; hard-core 400 m A/S = 8.76 -> DTI 0.10101; matched random A/S ~ 9.38 -> DTI 0.04291.
entries.disposition: open - src/gems55/emit_opt.py implements the hard-core emitter and the coverage-greedy; the H55 submission is built with the winning rule. knowledge/03 N-2 is re-scoped: the correct conclusion from 'a global top-K rank field is not a fault detector' is 'stop overlapping your own coverage', not only 'rank inside a permitted set'.

entries.title: Our own coverage-greedy wrote its running cover into a throwaway copy, and a test caught it
entries.what_it_is: src/gems55/emit_opt.py updated its running cover with `np.maximum(cf[nbi], kk, out=cf[nbi])`. Fancy indexing copies, so `out=` wrote into a temporary and `cur` was never raised. Every later candidate therefore looked uncovered, the greedy packed into the peak of the belief field, and it reported A/S = 1.8-2.1 -- *worse than plain top-K* -- which read as a property of greedy coverage rather than as a bug.
entries.how_we_know: tests/test_h53_emit.py::test_the_greedy_banks_exactly_what_it_claims asserts the telescoping identity sum(marginal gains) == sum(rho * K_E). It failed at 107.7 vs 66.6 on a 140x140 grid. After the one-line fix the greedy reaches A/S = 9.27 (98.8% of the 9.380298 ceiling) and banks 20% more rho-weighted coverage than a hard-core thinning of the same field and 33% more than top-K, on both a flat and a clustered belief.
entries.disposition: fixed - `cf[nbi] = np.maximum(cf[nbi], kk)`. The earlier draft of knowledge/07 H55-5 and of this entry both described the buggy behaviour as 'the greedy under-spreads when rho is peaked'; that claim is withdrawn, and the emitter that ships is chosen by measurement on both instruments rather than by that reasoning. Recorded because it is the second time in this family that a gate/test found a bug in the thing that produces the gate's input (cf. IR-52-007).

entries.title: The organiser's band-6 tag is contradicted by the survey contractor's own read-me: band 6 is radiometric total count, and the competition grid is node-aligned to the survey grid
entries.what_it_is: Band 6 of data/training_features.tif is tagged data_category = magnetic_data, 'Tilt angle or total curvature - magnetic field derivative for edge detection'. The GeoDAWN contractor read-me (NV5 / EDCON-PRJ, December 2022, Task Order 140G0221F0024) lists tc_raw and tccorr under Radiometrics and contains no tilt-angle channel anywhere in its channel inventory, so the tag does not correspond to any product the survey delivered. The same document gives the survey's Area 2 origin as 243200.0 / 4135400.0 at 100 m spacing, which is node-aligned to the competition grid rather than pixel-aligned.
entries.how_we_know: Two independent lines. First, the contractor read-me's own channel inventory. Second, measured on the bytes: Spearman(band 6, GeoDAWN total-count grid) = +1.0000; Spearman(band 6, K+Th+U) = +0.9915, which is what a total-count channel is by construction; and |Spearman| <= 0.148 against all five magnetic bands in the same file. Band 6 is also strictly positive (range 2.953 to 88.573), where a tilt angle is bounded by +/-pi/2. Independently corroborated by IR-52-019.
entries.handling: Band 6 is assigned to View B (as B_band6_TC), not to the potential-field view. A radiometric band inside View A would corrupt the conditional-independence test the two views are required to pass. Enforced by tests/test_r4.py::test_band6_is_in_view_b.

The arm is ABANDONED as a scored candidate.

entries.title: The prior family's per-cell credit allocation is under-determined; only an interval is knowable (credited-core alternate round)
entries.what_it_is: Thirteen owner-reported scores plus the |G| = 14,088.7 px anchor identify the family's total credit but not its per-cell allocation: 574 coverage patterns vs 13 equations. A linear program gives the honest interval for the 25,517-cell credited core: [4,079.1, 5,249.2] px of credit (0.5 % slack on the 4-decimal reported scores). Adding 'more detectors agreeing implies not-less credit' makes the system INFEASIBLE — the reported scores contradict that monotone-consensus model.
entries.how_we_know: evidence/gems57_credit_lp2.json, evidence/gems57_credit_robust.json, work/credit_lp.py (the coarser coverage-count model is also infeasible, same reason); scipy HiGHS linprog.
entries.disposition: Every projection in the README/site/knowledge is published as a bracket (0.227-0.336 for the shipped file), not as a point forecast. The pair identity T(ref) = T(d2-8) = 5,223.13 is still exact and is what pins the anchor.

entries.title: Three instrument defects produced confident wrong answers before they were caught
entries.observation: (1) Layers.matrix reshaped a layer-major memmap into a (layers*rows, cols) matrix; scikit-learn accepted it and reported 3,292 features instead of 39. (2) make_folds buffered on the component fold id, which is -1 off-catalogue, marking the whole grid as boundary and leaving 0 catalogue pixels in training on every fold. (3) The arm's legal set ANDed the catalogue visibility mask into the grid, restricting every arm to still-mapped faults; all arms then scored exactly 0.0000.
entries.handling: All three fixed in src/gems52/h57.py with a regression test for each the axis convention in particular, which had none.

entries.title: Portal rejection 'Predicted values must be in range [0, 1]' reported by the owner
entries.what_it_is: The owner reported the DrivenData validator rejecting a submission with exactly that message. Every raster this repository ever served as a primary download that could produce it is one carrying non-finite pixels — every comparison against a NaN is False, so a single such pixel trips the range check, and the historical '-nan' alias exports (knowledge/09) plus a research-only NaN-bearing alias previously linked prominently on the site match the error exactly.
entries.how_we_know: Re-read of the served artifacts: the shipped H59/H57/H56 canonical files are all-finite {0,1} (verified from bytes); the demoted alias tif re-reads with NaN outside the footprint; the error string is what the portal returns for both non-finite and out-of-range values.
entries.handling: The site now leads with one-click all-finite artifacts (docs/executive-summary.html), the NaN-bearing alias is demoted and labelled, and gems52.grid.write_geotiff refuses to emit non-finite/out-of-range arrays at the source, with the build's format gate verifying the re-read bytes. If the owner re-submits the exact H59 bytes (sha256 e884f84a...) and STILL sees the range error, that would be new information: this file provably contains only 0.0 and 1.0, so the rejection would then point at transport corruption or the wrong file being uploaded, and the owner-side sha256 check in the ZIP's STATUS.txt is the first diagnostic.
entries.status: mitigated at source - open until an owner upload of the H59 bytes confirms it
entries.disposition: Never ship a primary download that re-reads non-finite; verify the uploaded file's sha256 equals the receipt's before reporting any portal rejection as unexplained.

entries.title: Thirteen public scores cannot localise the hidden truth
entries.what_it_is: The metric linearises in a relaxed truth density, so 13 scores give 13 linear constraints. Under a uniform-truth assumption the implied |G| ranges from 11,349 to 499,618 across the 13 priors, with several priors admitting no solution; allowing the density to vary over 12,051 blocks with box bounds, the equality system is infeasible at every N from 1,000 to 60,000.

entries.what_it_is: data/scored/8GEMSDOE_Hedge-v2_submission.tif (736,494 bytes) and data/scored/gemsdoe-ens12-adopted-7f00890a.tif (570,890 bytes) differ in file size and compression but decode to exactly the same 227,507-pixel emission (|I & J| = 227,507 = |I| = |J|). Both are reported by the owner as 0.1563.
entries.how_we_know: Pixel-set comparison of the two restored rasters on the sample-submission grid; the H60 stage-2 pairwise overlap table.
entries.why_it_matters: It is the only internal consistency check available on the owner-reported file-to-score mapping: two artefacts with identical decoded content were reported with an identical score, so the mapping is at least self-consistent for this pair. It does NOT authenticate the mapping, because the board publishes no filename and both rows could be the same recording of one upload.
entries.handling: Treated as one file ('I', the GEMSDOE8 family) in every twelve-file computation, so the corroboration counts are not double-weighted.
entries.note: Distinct from main's same-numbered entry, which is preserved above under its original id.

entries.disposition: disclosed
entries.title: The twelve scored files are not jointly consistent: file C is a strict subset of file D yet reports a higher score
entries.what_it_is: C = gems24-d1-5 (60,069 px, 0.2477) is a strict subset of D = topo-gap-closure (61,328 px, 0.2449): measured C \ D = 0 px and D \ C = 1,259 px. Under the additive-atom model with M = T this requires the 1,259 extra pixels to carry -3.5 credit units, which is impossible.
entries.how_we_know: Exact set algebra on restored bytes, then T_i = score_i x (0.2 S_i + 0.8 |G|) with |G| = 14,088.7.
entries.why_it_matters: The raw LP is infeasible. A slack of max(4.0, 0.002 T_i) -- the smallest band that makes the system feasible -- is therefore applied to every equation and reported. It widens every identified interval slightly.
entries.handling: Intervals are computed with the slack and the slack size is published alongside them; no interval is reported as if the system were exactly consistent.

entries.disposition: disclosed
entries.title: Atom credit is set-identified, not point-identified; every non-file candidate set has a lower bound of zero
entries.what_it_is: Twelve equations in 559 unknown atom credits. Linear programming over the feasible polytope gives P1 = A n C credit in [4,132.6, 5,233.6] but gives A n I (4,814 px), E n I \ A (14,073 px) and cross-family sets a lower bound of exactly 0.
entries.how_we_know: scripts/h60_identify.py, per-set LP min and max with constraints t >= 0, sum t <= |G|, t <= 3|a|.
entries.why_it_matters: Any arm built from the priors has an UNMEASURABLE credit density. Earlier rounds reported NNLS point estimates for these same quantities, which select one corner of the polytope and invent information the organiser's scores do not contain.
entries.handling: Decisions are taken on intervals and the projection is published as a table over the arm-density prior, never as a single forecast.
entries.note: Distinct from main's same-numbered entry, which is preserved above under its original id.

entries.disposition: refuted
entries.title: The preregistered corroboration-ladder model is refuted by the organiser's own scores
entries.what_it_is: A four-coefficient model rho(c, f) = rho_clade * r_clade^(c-1) * r_ext^f fitted to the twelve measured credits reproduces them with median |relative error| 0.22, maximum 0.83, and leave-one-file-out median 0.28; file M is missed by a factor of 11 out of sample.
entries.how_we_know: scripts/h60_ladder.py, weighted least squares with 12 random restarts, plus a leave-one-file-out refit.
entries.why_it_matters: Corroboration count is not a sufficient statistic for credit density -- the same conclusion knowledge/03 N-10 reached by a different route ('habitat is not credit'). No arm may be sized on a corroboration-ladder argument.
entries.handling: Recorded as a refutation. The ladder was not used to size or rank the arm.

entries.disposition: disclosed
entries.title: |G| rests on a single nested pair, and publication rounding moves it by +/-70 px
entries.what_it_is: |G| = 14,088.7 px is solved from the single exact relation A subset B with the B \ A ring (6,436 px) carrying zero credit. Varying the two reported scores by one unit in the fourth decimal moves |G| by about 70 px.
entries.how_we_know: Analytic propagation: G = (score_B * 8818 - score_A * 7530.8) / (0.8 (score_A - score_B)).
entries.why_it_matters: Every credit and every density in the round scales with |G|. There is no second nested cross-family pair available to check it.
entries.handling: |G| is quoted to one decimal with the rounding band stated.

entries.disposition: fixed
entries.title: The out-of-fold fold assignment covered only catalogue pixels, so the independence test had zero blocks
entries.what_it_is: The first H60 co-training run assigned folds from connected components of the label raster only, leaving every non-catalogue pixel with fold 0. Out-of-fold probabilities were therefore undefined on exactly the labelled negatives the independence test needs, and the test reported blocks=0, rho=nan.
entries.how_we_know: Run log: 'blocks=0  rho=nan'.
entries.why_it_matters: A nan independence statistic would have been reported as 'premise not refuted', which is the wrong answer for the right-looking reason.
entries.handling: Folds are now a 200 px tile partition over the whole grid, assigned by (i + 2j) mod 4 so every 4-neighbour tile is in a different fold, with catalogue components forced whole into the fold of the tile holding their centroid.
entries.note: Distinct from main's same-numbered entry, which is preserved above under its original id.

entries.disposition: fixed
entries.title: The hide-and-recover survival check contradicted itself, and the first fold assignment emptied the training positives
entries.what_it_is: Two defects in the same block of code. (a) The training buffer was built from the training positives themselves (dilation of lab on the non-held folds), so 'lab and not buffer' was empty and clf.fit raised on a (0, 20) array. (b) The survival statistic divided the held-out truth by a buffer that by construction contained it, so survival always printed 0.000 while the emission set was in fact unrestricted.
entries.how_we_know: Run logs for both defects; the fix is the R4 section 4 rule that the held-out segment must be removed from the catalogue that builds the exclusion and must remain inside the placeable set.
entries.why_it_matters: (b) is the dangerous one: a printed survival of 0.000 would have invalidated every hide-and-recover number in the round while looking like a real result.
entries.handling: Buffer = dilation of the held-out fold only; survival = fraction of the held-out truth that lies inside the placeable candidate set.
entries.note: Distinct from main's same-numbered entry, which is preserved above under its original id.

A greedy-placed raster would therefore NOT externalize the measured field.

entries.disposition: disclosed
entries.title: Band 10 (dist_to_eq) carries distances larger than the grid can physically contain
entries.what_it_is: Inside the footprint, band 10 of data/training_features.tif has median 622.8 m and p99 50.2 km, which are plausible, but a maximum of 4,962,515 m. The grid is 3730 x 3292 px at 100 m, so its diagonal is about 492 km; 0.41% of footprint pixels (21,326 of 5,165,840) exceed 329 km and are therefore impossible as a distance-to-nearest-earthquake measured on this grid.
entries.how_we_know: Read band 10 directly with rasterio, applied the official nodata sentinel filter, and took percentiles over the 5,165,840-px footprint: min 0.0, p1 118.3, p50 622.8, p99 50,237.2, max 4,962,515.0, with mean(v > 329000) = 0.0041287.
entries.handling: Layers derived from band 10 are rank-encoded before any learner sees them, so the tail is compressed to a single extreme rank rather than dominating a linear model; the layer A_eq_dist_negrank is kept but must not be read as a physical distance. Flagged because any future use of band 10 as a metres-valued quantity (a buffer, a threshold, a decay length) would silently mis-handle those pixels.

entries.disposition: fixed; rule recorded
entries.title: Indexing a 2-D fold grid with one 1-D coordinate array allocated ~4 GB and was killed by the OOM killer with no traceback
entries.what_it_is: cotrain_r5.fit_oof did fold[rows] and fold[cols] on a (3730, 3292) int16 grid. With one index array numpy selects whole ROWS, so each expression built a (300k, 3292) view and the fold test broadcast over the wrong axis. On a 3.9 GB box the process was SIGKILLed (exit 137) during stage 2 with no Python traceback, which reads exactly like a memory-hungry model rather than like a two-character indexing bug.
entries.how_we_know: dmesg is the only place this sandbox records an OOM kill (/sys/fs/cgroup/memory.* is not exposed and free/ps mislead), plus an RSS watchdog that put the last allocation at cotrain_r5.py:194. Re-validated after the fix: view A out-of-fold in 41 s at 1,113 MB peak.
entries.handling: Paired indexing fold[rows, cols] everywhere, with the reason in a comment at the call site. Regression test in tests/test_r5.py. Standing rule: never index a 2-D grid with a single 1-D coordinate array.
entries.evidence: src/gems52_r5/cotrain_r5.py::fit_oof, logs/r5_main.log (local artifact; logs/ is gitignored)

entries.disposition: disclosed; published numbers are the reproducible ones
entries.title: Two runs of the same stage-3 code on the same on-disk fields logged different independence and A-only numbers, and both saved OOF fields carry 620 impossible zeros
entries.what_it_is: Run 1 logged spearman 0.15012 and A-only 43,604 px; run 2, loading the very files run 1 had just written, logged spearman 0.22757 and A-only 43,672 px. Separately, work/r5/oof_A.npy and oof_B.npy each hold 620 pixels with value 0.0 where they must be NaN: exactly row 0, columns 0-619, which is exactly the out-of-footprint prefix of the first row (valid turns True at column 620). Both files, same 620 pixels.
entries.how_we_know: Four checks, all in this checkout. (1) git diff 9bbcbf5..HEAD shows the only stage-3 code change between the two runs is inside pseudo_labels; independence, disagreement_strata and rank_within are untouched and RNG-free, and every input (cat 60,988 px, valid 5,165,840 px, legal 4,861,502 px, bid, pos, neg, seeded sample) is identical. (2) A fresh in-process recomputation from the saved arrays reproduces run 2 exactly (0.227574 spearman / 0.106752 pearson / A-only 43,672 / B-only 43,799). (3) The write path cannot touch those pixels: te_block = (fold == k) & valid, fold is -1 outside the footprint, and a fold-0 reproduction leaves the prefix fully NaN with no zero in its prediction vector. (4) np.save/np.load round-trips are exact here: a deterministic pattern, a NaN-heavy field, a re-save of oof_A.npy and two loads of it all agree bit for bit, so this is not file I/O. The mechanism is therefore unidentified.
entries.handling: Run 1's stage-3 log line is marked superseded and is not quoted anywhere in evidence/, docs/ or the site; every published stage-3 number comes from the arrays on disk and reproduces. The 620 pixels are outside the footprint, so no consumer can see them: rank_within masks to pos|neg, legal is a subset of valid, and the emission is a subset of legal. Bounded, not explained, and not papered over.
entries.provenance_warning: Any future stage-3 number must be recomputed from the saved fields and compared with the log before it is quoted.

entries.status: measured and reported; verdict NOT relaxed; prospective fix recommended to the shared selector
entries.title: The directed 3 px proximity rule has a chance level, and 31 registry rasters sit above its own trigger
entries.what_it_is: The statistic 'fraction of YOUR dots within 3 px of prior P' has chance level equal to P's own 3 px coverage of the eligible footprint: a uniformly random emission lands inside P's halo with exactly that probability. The rule's trigger is 0.70, so for any prior whose coverage is at or above 0.70 the rule fires on a random emission and cannot indicate lane drift. Measured over the 545-raster registry: 14 rasters have coverage >= 0.95 (probes under the preregistered policy) and 31 have coverage >= 0.70; of the 23 near-offenders, 14 are probes and all 9 informative ones have coverage 0.7583-0.8976 with NEGATIVE excess over chance (-0.0054 to -0.0291). Across all 545 priors the median excess is -0.0766 and only 108 are positive, i.e. the H61 emission is less clustered near prior dots than uniform chance. Max Spearman is 0.0361 (literal) / 0.0209 (policy) against a 0.90 trigger.
entries.how_we_know: scripts/h61_lane_analysis.py over evidence/h61_lane_dots.json (gems52.gates.lane_report on the written artefact, 545 rasters, 361 distinct decoded patterns), which itself measured per-prior coverage with gems52.gates.registry_coverage.
entries.handling: The preregistered probe threshold (0.95) and the literal 0.70/3 px rule were NOT relaxed: the recorded verdict stays DUPLICATE/STOP and the artefact stays research-only. The chance-normalised excess is published beside it so the reader can see that the STOP is a property of the registry's geometry, not evidence of a copied lane.
entries.disposition: Prospective fix for the shared selector, to adopt BEFORE the next round: apply the directed proximity rule only to priors whose measured coverage is below the rule's own trigger, or test the chance-normalised excess (near - coverage) against a margin. Both forms follow from the rule rather than being tuned to a result.

Independence held in both rounds (max |rho| 0.1331 / 0.1817), so the failure is sufficiency, not independence. The disagreement arm scored below uniform random in both rounds (H61 0.030584 vs random 0.080426; H63 0.040257 vs random 0.078257).
entries.how_we_know: evidence/h61_fit_checkpoint.json, evidence/h63_fit_checkpoint.json (sufficiency_screen), evidence/h61_holdout.json, evidence/h63_holdout.json (pooled scores and paired differences, 53,186 withheld positives, matched 9,400-dot budgets).
entries.handling: Recorded as a negative deliverable; the H63 artefact is published research-only (DOWNLOAD YES, SUBMIT NO, slots used 0). No re-tuning of either round into a positive result, and no promotion of either artefact. Round label renamed H62 -> H63 after a parallel session's H62 merged to main first (PR #46); the measured numbers are unchanged.
entries.disposition: Do not propose a third View-A parameterisation without new evidence (new data, a different splitter test, or an organiser-authenticated calibration). The lane's own falsification condition has fired twice; the next in-lane candidates are the B-only direction (H63-B) and the credit-localisation analysis (H63-E), both preregistered in knowledge/37 section 2.
